property_summary: For any caller with any approval status set via setApprovedLogger, the approvedToLog function must return the actual approval status in the reference contract, but the buggy version always returns false.
For any caller whose approval status has been set to true via setApprovedLogger, the reference approvedToLog returns true, but the buggy version returns false.
For any address that has been approved as a logger by the owner, approvedToLog must return true in the reference, but the buggy version always returns false.

For any address that is not an approved logger, approvedToLog must return false in both versions; the buggy version falsely returns false even when the address is approved, violating the rule that approval status is correctly reported.

For any caller and any approval status set by the owner, approvedToLog(caller) must return the exact approval status; the bug always returns false, so once the owner approves a caller the buggy contract reports false while the reference reports true.
setApprovedLogger can only be called by the contract owner

For any call to setApprovedLogger by the owner, the value of approvedLoggers for the given address must equal the _status parameter supplied; the mutant ignores _status and always sets it to true, so calling with _status=false fails this rule.

For any owner and any address logger, after setApprovedLogger(logger, false) returns successfully, the approvedLoggers mapping must reflect false; the mutant sets it to true regardless, violating this rule when false is passed.

For any owner call, after setApprovedLogger(logger, _status) completes, approvedLoggers(logger) must equal _status; the mutant always sets it to true, so any call with _status=false on an initially unapproved logger leaves a false approval invariant violated.

For any owner and any logger address, after calling setApprovedLogger(logger, false), approvedLoggers(logger) is false; the mutant always sets it to true, breaking this invariant when false is passed.

For any owner-set call to setApprovedLogger(logger, _status) with logger not currently approved, approvedLoggers(logger) must equal _status; the mutant breaks this when _status=false because it forces the mapping to true.
After a call to setApprovedLogger, the approval status of the given logger address must equal the input _status parameter; the bug always sets it to false regardless of _status.
After any call to setApprovedLogger, the approvedLoggers mapping for the given _logger must reflect the _status value, which the bugged version violates by leaving approvedLoggers unchanged.

After setApprovedLogger is called by the owner with any address and status, calling approvedToLog on that address must return the set status; the no-op mutant leaves approvedLoggers unchanged so approvedToLog returns false regardless of status when _status is true, breaking the rule.

For any call to setApprovedLogger by the owner, the approvedLoggers mapping for the given _logger must eventually equal _status; the no-op mutant leaves approvedLoggers unchanged, so a subsequent call to approvedToLog returns false when _status was true.

For any two back-to-back calls to setApprovedLogger by the owner with the same _logger but different _status, the final value of approvedLoggers(_logger) must equal the last _status set; the no-op mutant never updates approvedLoggers, so the final read returns the initial false regardless of the last _status.

For any two sequences of calls to setApprovedLogger by the owner with different loggers and statuses, the final approvedToLog for a logger set to true must be true; the no-op mutant never updates the mapping, so approvedToLog always returns false.
Only the contract owner can successfully change the approvedLogger status.

property_summary: For any caller, a successful call to setApprovedLogger must change the approvedLoggers mapping state; the buggy onlyOwner revert prevents any state update, leaving approvedLoggers unchanged.
After setApprovedLogger is called with any status, the stored value must equal the input status; the mutant inverts the logic, so the stored value is the opposite.

For any call to setApprovedLogger by the owner, the value of approvedToLog for that logger after the call must equal the boolean status parameter passed; the mutant inverts the storage, so the result equals !status.

After the contract owner calls setApprovedLogger with a given status, the value of approvedToLog for that logger must equal the input status; the mutant stores the opposite, so the stored value equals !status.

For any allowed caller and status, the stored approvedLoggers mapping for that logger after a successful setApprovedLogger call must equal the input status; the mutant inverts the boolean, so it reads as !status.

After a pranked owner calls setApprovedLogger, the value of approvedToLog for that logger must equal the input status; the mutant inverts the stored boolean, so it equals !status for any non-owner caller checking approvedToLog after the call.
After any call to setApprovedLogger, the logger's approval status must equal the _status argument; the buggy version always sets it to false, violating the rule.
After setApprovedLogger is called by the owner, an address that was granted approval remains approved for logging; the buggy version always revokes approval immediately after granting it.
For any owner call to setApprovedLogger with any address and status, the approvedToLog view of that address equals the given status after the call; the buggy version always sets it to false.

For any owner and any address, calling setApprovedLogger with _status=true followed by the same address with _status=false leaves approvedToLog false in the correct contract, but the order of calls never makes a difference in the buggy version because it always writes false.

For any owner call to setApprovedLogger with an address and status, the combined return value of the log* functions called by that address after the call (true if approved, false otherwise) must reflect the intended _status; the buggy version always revokes approval, making the log* functions return false regardless of _status=true.
After any call to setApprovedLogger, the mapping value for the logger must equal the input status parameter, but the bug makes it always false.
After an owner calls setApprovedLogger for any address with true, that address must have approvedToLog return true; the bug permanently sets it to false.

After the owner calls setApprovedLogger with _status=true for any logger, approvedLoggers[logger] must remain true as long as no subsequent setApprovedLogger call sets it to false, but the bug permanently forces it to false.

After the owner calls setApprovedLogger(logger, true), calling any log function as logger must not revert and should return true, but the mutant sets the logger's approval to false permanently, causing the log function to return false.

For any address not yet set as an approved logger, after the owner calls a sequence consisting of setApprovedLogger(addr, true) then setApprovedLogger(addr, any_bool), the final value of approvedLoggers[addr] must equal the second status; the bug always leaves it false irrespective of the second status.
Any account not approved by the owner cannot successfully emit the Created event through logCreated.
